name: llseek
synopsis: int syscall(SYS__llseek, unsigned int fd, unsigned long offset_high, unsigned long offset_low, loff_t *result, unsigned int whence);
description: The _llseek() system call repositions the file offset for the specified file descriptor to a 64-bit value formed by offset_high and offset_low, relative to the position defined by whence. It stores the new file offset in the provided result pointer. This call is primarily used on 32-bit platforms to handle large file offsets.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the open file to reposition

parameters.name: offset_high
parameters.description: High 32 bits of the 64-bit offset value

parameters.name: offset_low
parameters.description: Low 32 bits of the 64-bit offset value

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: Pointer to a location where the new file offset is stored

parameters.name: whence
parameters.description: Reference point for the offset (SEEK_SET for beginning, SEEK_CUR for current, or SEEK_END for end of file)

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: fd is not an open file descriptor
Problem with copying results to user space
